facts.text: Poplar became the tribal headquarters for the Fort Peck Indian Reservation after the military abandoned Camp Poplar in 1893.
The Poplar River joins the Missouri River near town, forming a confluence that early settlers used for trade.
Lewis and Clark camped near the Poplar River on May 3, 1805, about 3.5 miles upstream from its mouth.
The town hosts an annual Native American Pow Wow called Poplar Indian Days every first weekend in September, drawing dancers and drummers.
The Poplar Museum and Tribal Museum showcase tribal history and artifacts, preserving the heritage of the Assiniboine and Sioux tribes.
The area around Poplar attracted settlers as early as 1860 when Charles Larpenteur built a trading post at the confluence of the Poplar and Missouri rivers.
